scenes.say: Itchy eyes? Stop. Don't rub them. Here's what to do instead.

scenes.en: Dust, pollen or pet hair trigger an allergy. The eye releases histamine.
scenes.say: Why? Dust, pollen or pet hair trigger an allergy, and the eye releases histamine. That causes itching and redness.

scenes.en: Rubbing releases more histamine and makes it worse.
scenes.say: Don't rub. Rubbing releases even more of it, so the itch gets worse. Hard rubbing over time can also harm the clear front of the eye.

scenes.en: A clean, cool, damp cloth on closed eyes for a few minutes.
scenes.say: Do use a cool compress. Place a clean, cool, damp cloth over your closed eyes for a few minutes.

scenes.en: Wash hands and face after coming in. Change pillow covers often.
scenes.ta: வெளியே சென்று வந்ததும் கை, முகம் கழுவுங்கள்
scenes.say: Do wash your hands and face after coming in from outside, and change your pillow covers often.

scenes.en: Allergy usually affects both eyes. One red, painful eye is a different problem.
scenes.say: Did you know? Eye allergy usually affects both eyes and itches a lot. One red, painful eye is a different problem.

scenes.en: Pain, blurred vision, light sensitivity or thick discharge.
scenes.ta: வலி, மங்கல் பார்வை இருந்தால் உடனே மருத்துவரை பாருங்கள்
scenes.say: See an eye specialist urgently if you have pain, blurred vision, light sensitivity, or thick discharge.

scenes.en: Get your eyes checked. Free eye test in our store.
scenes.say: Itching that keeps coming back? Get your eyes checked. The eye test in our store is free.
